chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The elderly man and the one suffering from thirst, there is no blame upon them if they break their fast during the month of Ramadan, and each one of them should give charity every day with a mudd of food, and there is no making up (qada) for them. If they are unable (to give charity), then there is nothing upon them.'

key_terms.الشَّيْخُ الْكَبِيرُ: The elderly man (one who has reached an age where fasting becomes burdensome)
key_terms.الْعُطَاشُ: The one suffering from thirst/chronic condition
key_terms.مُدٍّ: A mudd (a traditional measure of volume, approx. 750g-1kg)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for elderly people or those with chronic illness who cannot fast during Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the ruling for the elderly and those with chronic, non-recovering conditions (al-‘utash), establishing that their exemption from fasting is permanent rather than temporary. Unlike those who fast temporarily due to illness, they pay fidyah (feeding a poor person) for each day missed without needing to make up the days (qada), reflecting the principle of ease in Shia jurisprudence. If financial hardship prevents payment, the obligation is entirely lifted, demonstrating the flexibility of divine law.
